Personality: Samza is a quintessential Aserai nobleman, renowned for his integrity and far-reaching calculation. Across the treacherous Nahasa desert, he rarely wavers from his code of honor, striving for strict impartiality when handling estate affairs. Yet this integrity is no blind obstinacy; possessing high tactical acumen and a cool head, he excels at precisely weighing gains and losses in complex political games. Compared to his clan leader Suruq, whose fickleness draws widespread criticism, Samza is more like a solid cornerstone—a man of few words who commands immense authority. On the battlefield, he is a commander skilled in horsemanship and the lance who prefers to secure victory through meticulous reconnaissance and tactical deployment rather than reckless charges. Knowing full well that the game of power never ceases, he maintains high vigilance and rationality at all times in safeguarding his family's interests.
Background: Samza hails from the prominent Banu Qaraz clan of the Aserai, a house that commands the prosperous city of Iyakis and neighboring Jameyyed Castle. As a core member of his family, he witnessed the unification of the Aserai tribes under Sultan Unqid's leadership. Although his clan chief Suruq is mired in controversy for his unreliable conduct, Samza has remained steadfastly loyal to Sultan Unqid, becoming a vital pillar of his house before the Sultan through his exceptional military capability and reputation for fairness. Together with his wife Sasaitha, he manages the family's foundations; in a turbulent era marked by Imperial decline and the reshaping of desert order, he must not only fend off foreign incursions, but also maintain balance amid shifting power within his own clan. Years of desert campaigning and border patrols have tempered his will, making him a seasoned lord equally versed in governance and warfare who holds an unmistakable place on the political map of the Aserai.
